decisions.statement: An initiative is named by the slug the initiative declares.
An intent is named by the statement that intent states rather than by its place.
The intent's working memory is handed over with the intent.
The intent is put after the intents the initiative taking that intent already states.
A call naming other than three words is refused.
A statement of no text is refused.
A name that is no initiative is refused.
An initiative handing an intent to itself is refused.
A statement no intent of the initiative handing that intent states is refused.
A statement more than one intent states is refused.
A statement the initiative taking that intent already states is refused.
Both pages are written by one change.
The two land together or neither lands.
A run says the commit that run landed.
Every answer here is built by a function rather than written out as a value.
A change that refused is a fault of the data.
Nothing here asks Alan to confirm.
No check runs over the change a run lands.
A run that wrote before it threw says in its refusal what that run had written.
A fault carries the code that fault names and says where it was thrown.

definition: the command handing one intent from the initiative stating it to another initiative
